e.meaning: her father, from a title of Fatimah
e.etymology: From Umm Abiha, mother of her father, a title of Fatimah, the Prophet Muhammad's daughter. The second word is used as a girl's name, mainly in Pakistan.
Mavi is the Turkish word for blue. In the US it is also used as a short form of Mavis, an old name for the song thrush, and of Maverick.
A spelling of Darren, a 20th-century name of unclear origin, possibly from an Irish surname. It spread in the 1960s through the character Darrin Stephens on the TV comedy Bewitched.
The Italian and Spanish form of Germanic Irmhild, from elements meaning whole and battle. Blessed Imelda Lambertini, a 14th-century girl of Bologna, spread it among Catholics.
namesakes: Imelda Marcos (former first lady of the Philippines, famed for her shoes)
Imelda Staunton (actress who played Dolores Umbridge in Harry Potter)

assoc.t: Imelda Marcos, Philippine first lady famed for her shoes

e.etymology: An American surname from French de Lannoy, of Lannoy, a place name meaning alder grove. It became a first name in honor of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, peaking in 1933.

assoc.t: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, whose middle name it was

e.etymology: A Latin American spelling of Giovanni, the Italian form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
A feminine form of the biblical name Adriel, Hebrew for flock of God, also read as Adrienne with the -elle ending of Arielle and Brielle.
A modern American coinage that adds the -lyn ending to Sky; a sister form of Skylar.
An Amharic name meaning one who is feared or respected. Tafari Makonnen was the birth name of Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia; with his title Ras it gave the Rastafari movement its name.
A spelling of Jayceon, a modern American elaboration of Jace or Jason with an -eon ending. Rapper The Game was born Jayceon Taylor.
A spelling of Myra, a name coined by the 17th-century English poet Fulke Greville, perhaps from Latin myrrha, myrrh, or as an anagram of Mary.
From Arabic ihsan, doing what is good and beautiful, from ahsana, to act well. In Islam ihsan is the ideal of worshipping God as though you could see him.
Latin for of India, a word used in the scientific names of many plants.

assoc.t: indica, one of the two main types of cannabis

e.note: Indica is best known as a type of cannabis and is sold under that name in dispensaries.

e.etymology: The feminine of Nazario, from Latin Nazarius, a person from Nazareth. Saint Nazaria Ignacia March Mesa, a Spanish nun who worked in Bolivia, was canonized in 2018.
A spelling of Remi or Remy, the French form of Latin Remigius, oarsman, the name of the bishop who baptized Clovis, king of the Franks.
A respelling of Kason or Kayson, modern American names in the rhyming family of Jason, Mason and Grayson.
A phonetic spelling of Veda, from Sanskrit veda, knowledge, the word for the oldest Hindu scriptures.
The form of Theodore used across Central and Eastern Europe and Scandinavia, from Greek Theodoros: theos, god, and doron, gift.
A Scottish surname, Gaelic Mac Ailein, son of Allan. Most Americans know it from The Macallan, a Speyside single malt Scotch whisky.

assoc.t: The Macallan, single malt Scotch whisky

e.etymology: A modern elaboration of Mila in the pattern of Malaya and Amaya. Mila comes from the Slavic element mil, dear or gracious, and milaya is Russian for dear one.
From Islay, an island in the Inner Hebrides known for its peaty whiskies. Isla is a form of the same place name, and in Scotland both are said EYE-luh.
e.note: The y is silent in Scotland, but many Americans will read the name as IZ-lay or EYE-lay.

assoc.t: Islay, Scottish island known for smoky single malt whisky

e.etymology: The name of Lucifer's angel brother in the TV series Lucifer, taken from Amenadiel, a spirit named in Renaissance-era books of magic. It follows the -el pattern of Hebrew angel names.

assoc.t: Amenadiel, the angel brother in the TV series Lucifer

e.etymology: A spelling of Jamal, from Arabic jamal, beauty. Both spellings became popular among African Americans in the 1970s.
An African American coinage that joins the prefix Key- to Shawn, the phonetic spelling of Irish Sean (John). NFL receiver Keyshawn Johnson made it widely known in the late 1990s.
namesakes: Keyshawn Johnson (NFL wide receiver and sports analyst)

e.meaning: pet form of Jonathan or John
e.etymology: A spelling of Johnny without the h, often because it is short for Jonathan, Hebrew for God has given, and not for John.
namesakes: Jonny Quest (boy adventurer of the Hanna-Barbera cartoon)

e.etymology: An English place name and surname, usually explained as broad settlement, from Old Norse breithr and Old English tun. As a first name it rides the wave of Brayden and Braxton.
A short form of Michael, from Hebrew Mikhael, who is like God? It is especially common in Ireland, Britain and Australia.
namesakes: Mick Jagger (lead singer of the Rolling Stones)
Mick Fleetwood (drummer and co-founder of Fleetwood Mac)

assoc.t: mick, an ethnic slur for an Irish person

e.note: Mick is also an old ethnic slur for an Irish person.

e.etymology: A form of Jibril, the Arabic name of the archangel Gabriel, from Hebrew Gavriel, God is my strength. In Islam Jibril is the angel who brought the Quran to Muhammad.

e.meaning: snow or happiness, depending on the kanji
e.etymology: A Japanese name whose meaning depends on the characters chosen: yuki can be snow or good fortune, and the long-vowelled boys' name Yuuki is often written as courage.
From Sanskrit tejas, sharpness, fire, radiance or spiritual brilliance.
e.note: Americans, especially Texans, may read it as Tejas (TAY-hahs), the Spanish name for Texas.

e.etymology: In the US mostly a variant of Kiana, the Hawaiian form of Diana that spread in the 1990s. Kiani is also a Persian surname meaning royal, after the legendary Kayanian kings.
